Dario and Sam are practically giving everyone an early taste of what it will be hearing from them in the form of earnings and sandbagging any future claims as both OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs are ahead of us.

Let's be real here, once you go public, everything you say is from the business side of the company and shareholder value. It's quite ironic we start hearing sandbagging takes, WHILE still hearing about profitable quarters from the companies as we enter IPO season for them.

Slowing down the pace of frontier models is simply another way for them to have the market value any future model they put out with more recognition and focus on margins. This has very little, if zero, influence from the safety of AI destroying humanity in my opinion. 

Both Dario and Sam know they are the ceiling setters for AI frontier models, and they are the ones who dictate the pace of the entire industry. If they want to slow down the pace, they can simply slow down the pace themselves. Applying regulations is just a way to create a monopoly on the frontier race, which in a sense, both OpenAI and Anthropic have already done. This is just another step to real dial into the monopoly edge. 

Slowing down the pace of frontier models being released does NOT mean training, memory, and compute usage goes down. There will still be rigorous amount of training, memory, inference, and investments needed. For some reason, people are taking slowing down pace of frontier models as a way of halting the entire operation. Regardless of how quick or slow you release a new frontier model to set a benchmark, it will still be going through heavy training throughout the entire time before being released. It's not as if frontier models will just halt all training. 

One could argue, with tighter regulations, comes even more training and investments to meet pre-release requirements.

What Dario and Sam are saying to the public is just the tip of the iceberg that gets seen by people. Where the real margins, compute, memory, and revenue sits is beneath the surface of the iceberg. 

Quite frankly, I believe this will create an environment where open-source, as well as closed-sourced juggernaut companies outside of OpenAI and Anthropic begin catching up which collectively increases the ceiling for AI, and comes the next big model from the big 2 in order to maintain their leads as they will then have become public companies. 

This new cycle will eventually create a new benchmark of demand for AI, NOT the other way around.
